Chris — great questions. See answers inline + attached artifacts (architecture diagram + a small eval CSV from a recent retail PoC).

Q1 — canonical flow:
- Option A (recommended initial): ES/BM25 -> candidate top_K (100) -> embed candidates -> rerank with neural ranker -> take top_N (5) to display. This gives strong recall while keeping reranker cost bounded.
- Option B (lower cost): embed query -> ANN search against vector index -> rerank top_K (50) -> top_N (5). Works well if you’re comfortable with vector index ops.

Q2 — top_k guidance:
- For support/FAQ: candidate K=100 from BM25 then rerank to top_N=5 is a common pattern. We often see diminishing returns beyond K=150 for these corpora.
- If latency is tight (P95 < 300ms): try K=50 and tune. Our internal benchmarks: K=100 -> +40–60ms on the reranker stage (depends on model size and batch settings).

Q3 — evaluation metrics:
- Offline: use MRR, NDCG@5, Recall@10. For retail FAQ content, target NDCG@5 > 0.55 and Recall@10 > 0.75 as initial benchmarks (these are heuristic; we can calibrate on your labels).
- Online: run an A/B where the reranker variant is evaluated on click-through and task success rate; also include a human-judged relevance set for sanity checks.

Q4 — auth/VPC routing:
- Hosted API: calls originate from your app to Redwood endpoints. For private routing we support VPC peering / Private Link so traffic never traverses the public internet. Auth is via API keys (KMS-friendly) and we can support mTLS for Dedicated/Private deployments. For a dev pilot inside your VPC, we can provide a test token and an allowlist of IPs or setup PrivateLink.

Attachments included: 2026-07-13-ava-retail-architecture-diagram.pdf (diagram), reranker-eval-results-20260713.csv (sample eval).

Action items:
- Dev: can you propose a pilot plan for a dev environment (short checklist: sample dataset, evaluation labels, ES export of candidate docs, and a test token)?
- Chris: pick 2–3 representative queries and a 200–500 doc sample we can use for the initial offline eval.

Hi Chris / Sam —

Quick technical note to help with the pilot setup. This is what we typically provide for a dev POC and should work inside your VPC with a test token.

1) Endpoints- Hosted inference endpoint (REST): https://api.redwood.com/v1/rank- Embeddings endpoint (REST): https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings

2) Auth- Use a scoped API key sent in Authorization: Bearer <KEY>. For PrivateLink/Dedicated we can swap to mTLS and customer-managed keys. For an internal dev pilot we’ll issue a short-lived test key with IP allowlist.

3) SDK snippet (nodejs) — thin wrapper around the REST endpoints:

const Redwood = require('@redwood-inference/sdk')
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })

async function rerank(query, candidates) {
  // compute embeddings for candidates or re-use your vector store embeddings
  const embResponse = await client.embeddings.create({ input: candidates })
  const rerankResponse = await client.rank.create({
    query: query,
    candidates: candidates,
    candidate_embeddings: embResponse.data,
    top_k: 50 // start here for pilot, tune to 100 if recall is low
  })
  return rerankResponse.top_results.slice(0, 5)
}

4) Performance knobs- Batch candidate embeddings to 32–64 to maximize throughput.
- Use our streaming/rerank endpoint with candidate_embeddings to avoid redundant embedding calls.
- If using GPU Dedicated, we can guarantee lower variability on P95.

5) Offline eval tips- Start with top_k=50 for the reranker and compute NDCG@5, MRR, and Recall@10. We can share a simple eval script if helpful.

If you can share the ES export (top 200 candidates for a handful of queries) to the Drive folder I linked, Ethan and I will run an initial eval and share the numbers.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if you want to walk through the SDK snippet.

—
